title: El Trampolín in Tamasopo: Complete Guide, Price and How to Get There (2026)
metaTitle: El Trampolín, Tamasopo: Free Entry, Guide & Directions
metaDescription: Complete 2026 guide to El Trampolín in Tamasopo: free entry, how to get there from Ciudad Valles, best hours, tips and what to see on the Agua Buena River.
excerpt: El Trampolín is a free river spot on the Agua Buena River in Tamasopo where you can swim and jump from the rocks. What it costs, the best hours and the exact route from Ciudad Valles.
contentHtml:
El Trampolín in Tamasopo (literally "the diving board") is a free-access natural spot on the Agua Buena River, in the municipality of Tamasopo, San Luis Potosí, where travelers of all ages come to swim and jump into the water from the rocky banks. Tamasopo is one of the most visited towns in the Huasteca Potosina, thanks to how close it is to Ciudad Valles — just 48 km on Mex-85 — and the many crystal-clear rivers around it. Many people confuse this spot with the Tamasopo Waterfalls park (Cascadas de Tamasopo), a separate paid venue, and end up unsure where exactly to go or how much money to bring. This guide clears that up once and for all: here you'll find everything about El Trampolín in Tamasopo, from the real cost of entry to the exact route from Ciudad Valles.

In the sections below you'll get to know El Trampolín on the Tamasopo River in detail: distances, landmarks, how it differs from the Tamasopo Waterfalls park, the best times of day to visit, and the tips we collect season after season from people who travel the Huasteca Potosina. According to records from local operators, in 2026 the Tamasopo area gets more than 8,000 visitors on high-season weekends (July and Holy Week, or Semana Santa), most of them drawn by its turquoise rivers.

At www.huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators in the region. This guide is updated with real experiences from people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: October 2026. El Trampolín in Tamasopo: what it is, where it is and why it's worth the trip

What exactly is El Trampolín in Tamasopo, and what can you expect when you get there?

El Trampolín in Tamasopo is an open stretch of the Agua Buena River where the rocks form natural ledges that visitors jump from into the river. There's no park infrastructure: no ticket booth, no water slides, no pools. What you'll find is clear blue-green water, a moderate current and a tree-lined bank that gives shade for much of the morning. Walking in is free; the only possible charge is an informal parking fee of around $20–$50 MXN, depending on the owner of the neighboring land, though it isn't fixed or guaranteed.

The groups we bring to this area usually combine El Trampolín with a visit to Puente de Dios or the Siete Cascadas (Seven Waterfalls), taking advantage of the fact that both sit along the same road. If you want to explore the region's rivers and canyons with an expert guide, the Water Route — Puente de Dios tour visits Puente de Dios and the Tamasopo Waterfalls from $1,500 MXN per person and includes round-trip transportation.

Is El Trampolín the same as the Tamasopo Waterfalls?

No. The Tamasopo Waterfalls are a private park with a ticket booth that charges $200 MXN per person in 2026. It has a palapa (thatched-roof shelter), a camping area and several stepped waterfalls that form pools for swimming. El Trampolín is a public spot on the same Agua Buena River, with no fences or tickets, just a few meters from the CBTA 141 high school after you cross the El Oro Bridge (Puente El Oro). The two are different and go well together: many travelers visit El Trampolín in the morning, when it's less crowded, and then pay to enter the park in the afternoon to see the waterfalls. For more on the waterfall park, see our complete guide to the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo.

How much does it cost to visit El Trampolín in Tamasopo, and when is the best time to go?

A free swimming spot in Tamasopo: what's included and what isn't

"Free swimming spot" describes El Trampolín perfectly: there's no fee to get into the river, no restrooms in the public area and no place to leave your things. What you get is one of the clearest stretches of the Agua Buena River, deep enough to jump safely from the banks. First-time visitors are often surprised by the water temperature, which stays around 22–24 °C in the dry season (November–April) and a bit cooler in July and August because of the rains.

The most important warning: in the rainy season (June–September), the river can rise quickly and loses its turquoise color from the sediment it carries. Operators in the region recommend avoiding El Trampolín on the days after heavy rain, especially if the water looks brown or the current is strong. Seeing the available tours in the Huasteca Potosina helps you plan a safe outing on confirmed dates.

Hours, crowds and the best time of day to go

Since it's a public space, El Trampolín has no official opening or closing hours, but daytime is the only sensible time to go: there's no lighting, and the rocky ground can be treacherous after dark. The ideal time is between 9:00 and 11:00 a.m., when the light filters through the trees, the water is calmer and most weekend visitors haven't arrived yet. On Saturdays and Sundays in July, the place can fill up from noon on with families from Ciudad Valles and San Luis Potosí. If you go on a weekday, you'll have the river practically to yourself. Local vendors selling aguas frescas (fresh fruit drinks) and snacks usually set up in the area from 10:00 a.m. on weekends, so if you arrive before then you'll find it quieter, with no crowds at the entrances.

According to local guides who work with us, in 2026 July weekends bring up to 400–500 people at a time to the whole Agua Buena area, including El Trampolín and the waterfall area. To compare the experience with other rivers in the Huasteca Potosina, read about Puente de Dios in Tamasopo, which is on the same route and is one of the most photographed spots in the Sierra Potosina.

Practical tips before visiting El Trampolín in Tamasopo

The difference between an easy visit and a complicated day usually comes down to logistics. These are the points travelers on our tours in the area mention most often:

  • Bring cash in small bills: the possible parking fee is cash only; there are no card terminals at the site. Set aside at least $100 MXN for it.
  • River-ready footwear: the rocks on the riverbed are slippery. Sandals with grippy soles or water shoes are a must; flat flip-flops get swept away by the current. Use the packing checklist for the Potosí jungle so you don't forget anything.
  • Avoid the heavy-rain season: between June and September the river can rise within hours. Check the local forecast before you go; if it rained in the mountains the day before, postpone your visit. Our article on the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina gives you the month-by-month picture.
  • Biodegradable sunscreen: the rivers of the Huasteca Potosina are sensitive ecosystems. Use mineral or biodegradable sunscreen so you don't pollute the water; some parks in the region already require it by regulation.
  • Suggested minimum budget per person: $300–$400 MXN to cover gas or transportation, parking, snacks and a meal at the Tamasopo market, where a plate of enchiladas or barbacoa runs about $80–$120 MXN.

How do you get to El Trampolín in Tamasopo from Ciudad Valles?

The route from Ciudad Valles to El Trampolín is direct and well signposted for most of the way. The groups we organize from Ciudad Valles make the trip in 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, depending on traffic leaving the city and on the Tamasopo stretch. The road is paved the whole way, although the last kilometer to Agua Buena can have potholes in the rainy season, so take it slow.

Step-by-step route: from Ciudad Valles to Agua Buena

From Ciudad Valles, take federal highway Mex-85 north toward Tamasopo. When you reach downtown Tamasopo, continue on the road to Agua Buena for about 4–5 km. The key landmark is the El Oro Bridge (Puente El Oro): as soon as you cross it, you're in the village of Agua Buena. Less than 50 meters past the bridge you'll see the entrance to El Trampolín on your right, right across from CBTA 141. There's no big official sign, but parked cars and families walking toward the river are a sure sign you've arrived. If you're taking public transportation from Ciudad Valles, catch a combi (shared van) to Tamasopo from the bus station; it costs about $40–$60 MXN each way.

Transportation options to get to El Trampolín on the Tamasopo River

You can get there by car or by public transportation, but the combi will drop you off in downtown Tamasopo, and from there you'll need a mototaxi or a walk of the remaining 4–5 km to Agua Buena. Mototaxis charge around $50–$80 MXN per person to the El Trampolín entrance. For groups coming from Xilitla or San Luis Potosí, the distance is longer, but the road runs through mountain scenery that makes the trip worth it on its own. Frequently asked questions about El Trampolín in Tamasopo

Is El Trampolín in Tamasopo free to visit in 2026?

Yes. El Trampolín is a public spot on the Agua Buena River and doesn't charge admission. In 2026 there may be an informal parking fee of $20 to $50 MXN, but it isn't mandatory or fixed. Don't confuse it with the Cascadas de Tamasopo park, which does charge $200 MXN per person.

How much money should I bring to visit El Trampolín on the Tamasopo River?

With $300–$400 MXN per person you'll cover transportation from Tamasopo, parking and a meal at the local market. If you're driving your own vehicle from Ciudad Valles, add about $120–$160 MXN in gas for the round trip. There's no ATM at the site, so bring cash.

What's the best time of year to visit El Trampolín in Tamasopo?

The dry season, from November to May, is ideal: the Agua Buena River is turquoise, the water level is steady and the currents are manageable. In July and August you can still visit El Trampolín, but the river can get less clear after rain. Holy Week and July are the busiest times.

Is El Trampolín in Tamasopo safe for families with kids?

With adult supervision and in the dry season, yes. The pools are deep enough to swim and jump, but check the current before letting children go in on their own. El Trampolín has no lifeguards or depth markers, so water shoes and life jackets for the little ones are highly recommended. Skip the visit if the river is murky or running high.

Can I combine El Trampolín with the waterfall park on the same day?

Yes, and it's the most common combination for visitors coming from Ciudad Valles. Ideally, get to El Trampolín between 9:00 and 11:00 a.m., when it's less crowded and the light is better for photographing the turquoise water. Afterward you can walk or take a mototaxi to the entrance of the Cascadas de Tamasopo park, which opens at 8:00 a.m. and closes at about 5:00 p.m.. Allow at least 2 hours per site to enjoy them without rushing, and save some energy for the trip back.
